title: Diagnosing Cache and Artifact Problems knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Diagnosing Cache and Artifact Problems?
options: Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
When an artifact is missing or a cache misses, inspect upload/download paths, artifact names, run/job boundaries, keys, restore behavior, and retention.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
questions.answer_key: When an artifact is missing or a cache misses, inspect upload/download paths, artifact names, run/job boundaries, keys, restore behavior, and retention.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of diagnosing cache and artifact problems: When an artifact is missing or a cache misses, inspect upload/download paths, artifact names, run/job boundaries, keys, restore behavior, and retention. Validate configuration and behavior against the current official reference before production use.

questions.prompt: How should a reviewer verify a change related to diagnosing cache and artifact problems?
options: Publish the workflow to production before reviewing its triggers and permissions.
Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
Assume the workflow is correct as soon as the YAML file is committed.
Retry every failure without looking at the exit code or preserving evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.explanation: Reliable verification uses observable evidence. For this lesson, consider: When an artifact is missing or a cache misses, inspect upload/download paths, artifact names, run/job boundaries, keys, restore behavior, and retention. A syntax check alone cannot prove remote execution, permissions, or deployment behavior.
